facts.value: Greater Lincolnshire Combined County Authority (GLCCA) — a separate statutory body, inaugural year 2025/26; operates treasury under Service Level Agreement with North East Lincolnshire Council (NELC)

source.title: GLCCA's Treasury Management Strategy Report — Authority meeting, 25 February 2026 (Agenda Item 9)

facts.note: IMPORTANT: this is NOT Lincolnshire County Council. E10000019 is Lincolnshire CC's GSS; the disk filing is a convenience. Any email must address GLCCA specifically. The report is signed by Debbie Simpson (Interim S73 Officer, GLCCA) but the named contact officer is Gary Bennett at NELC (gary.bennett@nelincs.gov.uk), because NELC provides the treasury service under SLA.

facts.value: £0.0m at 31.12.2025 — no PWLB (fixed or variable), no LA borrowing, no market loans, no LOBOs

source.title: Appendix A – GLCCA Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27, Annex 1 (p.35)

facts.note: Table shows every category at 0.0. GLCCA is in its inaugural year and has taken no external debt of any kind. S73 Overview (Appendix A p.4): 'The Authority currently has no plans to borrow for its Capital Programme and has no maturing debt so this Strategy ... focusses on Investments and cash flow.'

source.title: Appendix A – GLCCA Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27, Prudential Indicators (p.28, p.32)

facts.note: Capital programme is 100% grant-funded across all four years (Total Expenditure: £134.1m / £132.9m / £151.2m / £167.8m; Government Grants same in every year; Borrowing 0.0 in every year). No CFR is generated, therefore no MRP charge falls.

facts.value: No PWLB loan record exists for GLCCA in our file
facts.note: OUR figure, verified with price_book.py --find on 'LINCOLNSHIRE' (returns Lincolnshire County Council, Lincolnshire Police & Crime Commissioner, North East Lincolnshire, North Lincolnshire — none of them the CA), on 'GREATER' (Greater London, Greater Manchester CA + its debt admin fund only) and on 'COMBINED' (eight combined bodies, none Greater Lincolnshire). Both sides tie at zero, but this is not a meaningful reconciliation in the ordinary sense — it is confirmation that a brand-new CA has taken no PWLB. Nothing to price.

facts.value: £32.2m at 31.12.2025 at average rate 3.71% — all short-term, in-house managed

source.title: Appendix A – GLCCA Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27, Annex 1 (p.35) and Investment Strategy (p.13, p.21)

facts.note: 2025/26 balances ranged £8.1m to £37.5m (p.13). Investment income budget for 2026/27 is £1m. Forecast average returns: 2026/27 3.25%; 2027/28 3.00%; 2028/29 2.75%. Portfolio credit rating target: A. Minimum liquidity reduces from £10m in 2025/26 to £5m for 2026/27. £10m single-counterparty limit ex-UK Govt against a ~£32m portfolio implies ~31% single-name concentration by design.

facts.value: Authorised Limit for external borrowing cut from £280m (2025/26, inherited NELC strategy) to £5m for each of 2026/27, 2027/28 and 2028/29

source.title: Appendix A – GLCCA Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27, Prudential Indicators (p.34)

facts.note: Operational Boundary for external debt goes to zero for 2026/27–2028/29 (from £250m in 2025/26). This is the loudest structural signal in the paper — a member-level statement of intent that GLCCA does not intend to borrow within the three-year horizon. Overview & Scrutiny (28 January) noted the 'zero-borrowing approach' as 'temporary while the Authority establishes its financial position' (covering report p.59 §12).

facts.value: Advisor central case (Arlingclose, Dec 2025): Bank Rate 3.75% → 3.25% by Dec-26, flat through Mar-29. 5yr PWLB 4.50% (Mar-26) → 4.10% (Mar-27, held to Mar-29); 10yr 5.20% → 4.70%; 25yr 5.80% → 5.20%; 50yr 5.60% → 5.00%.

source.title: Appendix A – GLCCA Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27, External Context (p.8)

facts.note: Dated, falsifiable central case. The forecast underpins their statement that 'The Authority is not exposed to borrowing rate risks this year' — but the market has moved AGAINST the term forecast in every bucket since. As at 2026-08-14 (PWLB notice 314/26 PM, certainty rates): 5yr 5.34% (+0.84 vs Mar-26 forecast); 10yr 5.83% (+0.63); 25yr 6.46% (+0.66); 50yr 6.27% (+0.67). Bank Rate is at 3.75%, matching Mar-26 forecast (BoE cut on 18 December 2025, which the paper itself acknowledges). Balance of risks flagged upside in the paper (p.9). Not a criticism — GLCCA plans not to borrow, so the move is a rates-outlook data point, not a P&L one. But it is testable, it is theirs, and it makes the strongest opening for a first-contact email.

source.title: Appendix A – GLCCA Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27, Prudential Indicators (p.32)

facts.note: Negative because GLCCA is a net investor — no debt interest, £1m investment income budget for 2026/27. The narrowing (25/26 -2.03% → 27/28 -1.84%) then widening (28/29 -3.09%) is likely a denominator effect on a small and volatile net revenue stream, not a policy signal. Do not read this as a return of borrowing.

facts.value: Liability Benchmark chart shows Loans CFR at zero and net loans requirement flat and negative at approximately -£45m to -£47m through the 60-year forecast to 2096

source.title: Appendix A – GLCCA Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27, Local Context (p.10) and Prudential Indicators – Liability Benchmark (p.33)

facts.note: Reflects the current no-borrowing stance and no future MTFP-period reserves changes. The paper explicitly warns (p.33) that 'Should that position change, before new long-term borrowing is entered into the Authority will have regard to the revised Liability Benchmark'.

facts.value: Non-specified investment ceilings: total long-term (>366 days) £5m; unrated or below A- (ex other LAs) £1.5m; foreign non-AA+ £1.5m; total non-specified £14m. Single-counterparty limit ex-UK Government £10m per organisation for <366 days. LA sector cap 30% of overall balances (£12bn national inter-LA market cited from Arlingclose, March 2025).

source.title: Appendix A – GLCCA Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27, Investment Strategy tables 2–4 (p.17, p.23, p.24, p.25)

facts.note: The £5m long-dated ceiling matches the £5m long-term investments line on the non-specified table and the £5m Upper Limit on fixed interest rate exposure (p.27). Deposits <366 days count as variable-rate exposures. Reserves available to cover investment losses ~£24m at 31 March 2027 (p.23) — the £10m per-name cap sits at ~42% of that, in line with the paper's own 'no more than 50% of available reserves at risk on a single default' rule.

facts.value: Annuity method at the average relevant PWLB rate for the year of expenditure, over asset life, starting the year after operational. Freehold land 50 years; investment property 50 years; regulation-capitalised 20 years; IFRS 16 matches rent charge. Cumulative VRP at 1 April 2025: £0.0m. No VRP proposed for 2026/27.

source.title: Appendix A – GLCCA Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27, Annex 2 – Annual MRP Statement (p.36–37)

facts.note: No MRP charge actually falls in the strategy period because there is no borrowing-funded expenditure. Policy is drafted for a future in which that changes.

facts.value: Companion paper 72316 (Agenda Item 10) approves updates to Treasury Management Practices: GLCCA bank details added; Arlingclose treasury adviser details added; additional brokers added; oversight adjusted so Scrutiny reviews policy/processes and Audit reviews control-environment performance.

source.title: Treasury Management Practices covering report — Authority meeting, 25 February 2026 (Agenda Item 10)

facts.note: Second contact address surfaced on this paper: Debbie Simpson, Interim S73 Officer, Debbie.Simpson@greaterlincolnshire-cca.gov.uk — GLCCA's own domain, distinct from the NELC address on the TMSS paper. Appendix A 72317 is 38pp of standard CIPFA TMP boilerplate with no material new figures.

facts.value: none (verified quiet — read; no distress, no debt, all prudential indicators comply)

source.title: Appendix A – GLCCA Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27

facts.note: This is a 'we read it and nothing alarms' record. The interesting content is structural (zero-borrowing intent) and forecast-vs-actual (Dec-25 rate view already beaten to the upside on term rates), not risk-flagged.

summary.text:
This paper is Greater Lincolnshire Combined County Authority's 2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy, approved on 25 February 2026. It is filed on disk under E10000019 (Lincolnshire County Council's GSS) as a convenience, but GLCCA is a separate statutory body in its inaugural year, operating treasury under a Service Level Agreement with North East Lincolnshire Council. Any email must address GLCCA specifically — Lincolnshire CC's PWLB book is a different body's book.

The 2025/26 strategy inherited NELC's — Authorised Limit £280m, Operational Boundary £250m. The 2026/27 strategy collapses those to £5m and zero respectively for each of the next three years. That is the loudest structural signal in the paper: a member-level statement that GLCCA does not intend to borrow within the three-year horizon. Overview & Scrutiny (28 January) noted this is 'temporary while the Authority establishes its financial position' but the numbers are what they are. CFR is zero across all four years. The £134.1m/£132.9m/£151.2m/£167.8m capital programme is 100% government grant funded.

Annex 1 at 31.12.2025 shows every external-debt category at £0.0m — no PWLB fixed, no PWLB variable, no LA borrowing, no market loans, no LOBOs. Investments were £32.2m in-house at an average 3.71%. Our own PWLB file confirms — GLCCA does not appear in any of the borrower-name searches we ran. Reconciliation ties trivially at zero. It is not the meaningful match a debt-holding council gives; it is confirmation that a brand-new CA has taken no PWLB.

The one dated, falsifiable statement in the paper worth surfacing is the Arlingclose interest-rate forecast from December 2025 (p.8): Bank Rate 3.75% → 3.25% by end-2026, then flat; 5yr PWLB 4.50% at Mar-26 falling to 4.10% by Mar-27; 25yr 5.80% falling to 5.50%. Bank Rate has held at the Mar-26 level (Bank of England cut to 3.75% on 18 December 2025, which the paper acknowledges). Term rates have gone the OTHER way — as at 14 August 2026 PWLB certainty rates are 5.34% at 5yr (+0.84), 5.83% at 10yr (+0.63), 6.46% at 25yr (+0.66), 6.27% at 50yr (+0.67). Not a P&L point for a body that plans not to borrow, but the strongest opening we have.

The balance-sheet identity ties at zero: CFR (£0) − external borrowing (£0) − other LT liabilities (£0) = internal borrowing (£0). No MRP charge falls because there is no borrowing-funded expenditure. Financing costs to net revenue is negative across the horizon (-2.03% / -2.15% / -1.84% / -3.09%) because GLCCA is a net investor — the 28/29 widening is a denominator effect on a small net revenue stream, not a policy signal.

Two contact addresses are published on the two papers considered at 25 February. Gary Bennett (Credit and Investment Manager, NELC, gary.bennett@nelincs.gov.uk) is the named contact on the TMSS report — he is the NELC-side treasurer running GLCCA's day-to-day treasury under SLA. Debbie Simpson (Interim S73 Officer, GLCCA, Debbie.Simpson@greaterlincolnshire-cca.gov.uk) is the statutory officer, named on the TMP report at the same meeting. Both are legitimate; Gary owns the paper we're writing about; Debbie owns the statutory role. Suggest sending to Gary and cc'ing Debbie.

Signal: none. This is a 'we read it and nothing alarms' record — no distress, no debt, prudential indicators all comply.

The PWLB: what you can and can't do with it
officer.body:
Hi Gary,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. Normally that means we open with a loan-book reconciliation — we hold N loans totalling £X against the £Y in your Table N — and then a couple of observations. GLCCA's is going to be a bit shorter, because your 25 February strategy is honest that the Authority has no borrowing, no CFR and no maturing debt, and the whole document 'focusses on Investments and cash flow'. Our own PWLB file agrees at zero. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and this is a first read of a paper, not a critique.

The one place a lender's eye lands on your strategy is the Arlingclose rate forecast on page 8, dated December 2025. That's the passage that underpins the sentence 'The Authority is not exposed to borrowing rate risks this year'. Bank Rate has held where you put it — 3.75% at March, matching the Bank of England's 18 December cut you note on the same page — but term rates have moved the other way. Your Mar-26 5-year is 4.50%; certainty on notice 314/26 (14 August) is 5.34%. Your 10-year 5.20% is at 5.83%. Your 25-year 5.80% is at 6.46%. Your 50-year 5.60% is at 6.27%. Roughly 60 to 85 basis points higher across every term bucket. Not a P&L point for an authority whose strategy is not to borrow; but it is the reason the CIPFA Prudential and Treasury Code updates are pushing the liability benchmark to the front of every committee paper, so that if the policy did change the tool for testing 'what would we pay today' is on the table before the decision. Our rates page carries both fixings daily and the certainty overlay is on by default; it's at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-rates.

The other structural thing worth flagging is the Authorised Limit, which steps from £280m in the inherited 2025/26 strategy to £5m for each of the next three years, with Operational Boundary at zero. That reads to us as a clear member-level statement, not a placeholder — the sort of decision Scrutiny asked about on 28 January when they described the zero-borrowing approach as 'temporary while the Authority establishes its financial position'. Where other combined authorities have gone the other way (Greater Manchester, Tees Valley, West Midlands and North East all have PWLB positions in our file) the sector context might be useful reading; our monthly loans-drawn breakdown is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity, and July's number was £368m across 33 loans from just 19 borrowers at an average 5.02%, which shows how thin the market has become at the point authorities do come in.

On training, three would fit the papers you're likely to see next. Liability Benchmark: the essentials, because the paper's own p.33 warning is that any change of position will trigger a revised benchmark before new borrowing. Prudential and Treasury indicators for members, because the Authorised Limit and Operational Boundary movements this year are the sort of vote that benefits from a common member framing. And The PWLB: what you can and can't do with it, offered for the day the Authority does turn to it. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: GLCCA's Treasury Management Strategy Report and its Appendix A (which carries the figures cited above), Authority meeting 25 February 2026 — https://lincolnshire.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s72320/glcca-s-treasury-management-strategy-report.pdf
